title: Did You Know Ice Cream Has a Whole Month Just for It?
summary: What's your favorite ice cream flavor? Vanilla? Chocolate? Maybe something wild like mint chocolate chip? Well, July is the perfect time to grab a scoop because it's National Ice Cream Month! This cool celebration started way back in 1984 when President Ronald Reagan decided ice cream deserved its own month. He even made the third Sunday of July National Ice Cream Day. Talk about a sweet idea! But ice cream has been around for way longer than that. The very first frozen dessert like ice cream was made in China over 1,000 years ago during the Tang Dynasty. It was made with milk, flour, and something called camphor — not exactly the sprinkles and hot fudge we love today! A more modern version using milk and sugar came from Arab chefs in the 9th century. Ice cream didn't reach America until 1744, when a governor in Maryland served strawberry ice cream at a fancy dinner. Everyone went crazy for it. Even George Washington spent a huge amount of money — about $200 in one summer — on ice cream. That was a fortune back then! For a long time, only rich people could enjoy it because ice was hard to store. Then in 1851, the first ice cream factory opened in Pennsylvania, and suddenly everyone could get a taste. Today, Americans eat about 23 pounds of ice cream per person every year. That's like carrying around a heavy bag of dog food made of ice cream! California makes the most ice cream, but the biggest fans live in Rhode Island, Wisconsin, and Washington, DC. And get this: your favorite flavor might say something about you. A scientist found that vanilla lovers are adventurous, chocolate fans are outgoing, and strawberry people are thoughtful. The world's biggest ice cream scoop was made in Wisconsin in 2014 — it weighed over 3,000 pounds and was taller than a grown-up! Now that's a sundae.
why_it_matters: Ice cream is a treat you can share with friends and family, and its story shows how a food that was once only for kings and presidents became something every kid can enjoy.

background_read: Before freezers, people had to cut ice from frozen lakes in winter and store it underground to keep it cold all summer, so ice cream was a rare treat only for the rich.
President Ronald Reagan (the U.S. president from 1981 to 1989) created National Ice Cream Month in 1984, and many other presidents have also named special food days.
The first ice cream recipe in English was published in the 1700s, and George Washington (America’s first president) was known to love ice cream and spent a lot of money on it.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Ronald Reagan and ice cream fans across America.
WHAT: July is National Ice Cream Month, a celebration that started in 1984.
WHERE: In the United States, with ice cream history stretching back to China, the Middle East, and early America.
WHY: Reagan felt ice cream deserved recognition, and after factories made it cheap, everyone could enjoy it.

perspectives.description: Ice cream month is a fun way to enjoy a favorite dessert with family and friends, with festivals and special deals.
Some worry that having a whole month for ice cream might make people eat too much sugar, which isn't healthy.
The story shows how technology, like factories and refrigeration, turned a luxury into an everyday food that almost anyone can afford.
